name: smr-data-centers
question: Are small modular nuclear reactors economically competitive for powering large AI data centers?

academic.title: Levelized cost projections for small modular reactors: a systematic review
academic.abstract: We review 42 published cost estimates for small modular reactors (SMRs) and find a median projected levelized cost of electricity of $120 per megawatt hour, with estimates from vendors clustering substantially below those from independent analysts. Estimates that account for first-of-a-kind effects are roughly twice those that do not.

academic.title: Historical cost escalation in nuclear construction, 1970-2020
academic.abstract: Using a database of 349 reactor construction projects we show that realized overnight construction costs exceeded initial estimates by a median of 117 percent, and that escalation was persistent across vendors, regulatory regimes and decades.

academic.title: Learning rates and modular construction: evidence from shipyard analogues
academic.abstract: Factory fabrication has produced learning rates of 8 to 12 percent per doubling in shipbuilding and modular construction. We argue that transferring these rates to reactor manufacturing requires order books an order of magnitude larger than any announced SMR pipeline.

academic.title: Data center load growth and firm generation requirements for AI workloads
academic.abstract: We model hyperscale data center load growth under three AI deployment scenarios and find that firm capacity requirements are met most cheaply by a combination of gas, storage and demand response through 2035 under current reactor cost assumptions.

academic.title: Negative learning in the French nuclear programme
academic.abstract: Costs in the French standardized reactor programme rose rather than fell with cumulative experience, a pattern we term negative learning and attribute to scale-up, regulatory ratcheting and loss of construction expertise.

academic.title: Why small modular reactor cost estimates are systematically optimistic
academic.abstract: Vendor cost estimates for SMRs omit first-of-a-kind engineering, assume construction schedules never achieved in the West, and rely on order volumes that no announced pipeline supports. We find no empirical basis for the claim that modularity will reverse historical cost escalation.

academic.title: Rapid cost declines in factory-built reactor components
academic.abstract: We report cost declines of 40 percent per doubling in factory-built reactor components. (Retracted: the underlying cost dataset could not be verified by the publisher.)

NuScale and utility group terminate flagship small modular reactor project

WASHINGTON (Reuters) - NuScale Power and the Utah Associated Municipal Power Systems said on Wednesday they had agreed to terminate the Carbon Free Power Project, the flagship small modular reactor plant that was to be built at the Idaho National Laboratory.

The companies said subscription levels from participating utilities were insufficient to proceed. The target price for power from the plant had risen to about $89 per megawatt hour from $58 per megawatt hour in earlier estimates, an increase the partners attributed to inflation in materials and higher interest rates.

Analysts said the cancellation was a setback for a technology that developers have promoted as a faster, cheaper route to new nuclear capacity, including for large data centers being built for artificial intelligence workloads.

NuScale said it would continue to pursue other customers and that its design remained the only small modular reactor design approved by the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission.

Tech companies sign nuclear power agreements for AI data centers

A group of technology companies has signed a series of agreements to buy electricity from planned nuclear projects, betting that reactors can supply the round-the-clock power that artificial intelligence data centers require.

The agreements are structured as power purchase commitments rather than construction financing, according to two people involved in the negotiations who were not authorized to discuss them publicly. None of the projects has begun construction, and several depend on reactor designs that regulators have not yet certified.

Utility analysts cautioned that announced capacity is not the same as delivered capacity. Data center operators have also signed agreements for gas generation and grid upgrades covering the same load, and those contracts are further along.

See the NRC design approval notice and the company's annual report.

Tech giants are betting on nuclear for AI

Tech giants are turning to nuclear power for their AI data centers, according to a report published this week.

The agreements are reportedly structured as power purchase commitments rather than construction financing. None of the projects has begun construction, and several depend on reactor designs regulators have not yet certified, the report said.

What this means for the industry is still unclear, but the deals signal that data center operators see firm generation as a constraint on AI expansion.

NRC issues standard design approval for small modular reactor

The U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission has issued a standard design approval for the 77-megawatt-electric small modular reactor design.

The approval covers the design only. An applicant seeking to build and operate a plant using this design must still obtain a combined license, which requires site-specific review including environmental and emergency planning analyses.

The staff's safety evaluation report identifies no unresolved safety questions for the certified scope.

We have not yet completed construction of any commercial plant, and we have generated no revenue from power sales.

Our estimated cost of electricity for a first-of-a-kind plant is subject to material uncertainty. Estimates assume construction durations, financing costs and supply chain pricing that have not been demonstrated at commercial scale, and prior estimates have been revised upward.
